Based on soil analytical results, remaining hydrocarbon impacts above regulatory standards have been successfully mitigated. Consequently, Kerr-McGee is requesting a No Further Action (NFA) determination for this location. On April 8, 2013, a historic release was discovered below the produced water vessel at the Noffsinger 1-17 production facility. The lateral and vertical extent of the excavation was determined by field screening of volatile organic compound (VOC) concentrations using a photoionization detector (PID). Approximately 100 cubic yards of impacted material were removed and transported to the Waste Management Facility in Ault, Colorado for disposal. Groundwater was not encountered during excavation activities. At the time of the release, the COGCC did not require a 72-hour notification of historic impacts if groundwater was not encountered. In addition, a Form 27 P&A request was considered sufficient in providing historic spill information, excavation, and environmental sampling activities. Consequently, a Form 19 was not submitted in 2013 following the release discovery.
Area Depth Determined: Excavation activities were completed on April 8, 2013, following the discovery of a historic release below the produced water vessel during plug and abandonment activities. Approximately 100 cubic yards of impacted material were removed and transported to the Waste Management Facility in Ault, Colorado for disposal. Soil samples were collected from the base and sidewalls of the excavation area at approximately 20 feet and 15 feet below ground surface (bgs), respectively. Samples were submitted to Summit Scientific Laboratories (Summit) in Golden, Colorado for analysis of benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and total xylenes (BTEX), naphthalene, and total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) - gasoline range organics (GRO) by USEPA Method 8260B, and TPH - diesel range organics (DRO) by USEPA Method 8015. Analytical results indicated constituent concentrations were in exceedance of COGCC Table 910-1 standards in soil samples collected from the south sidewall (SS03), west sidewall (SS04), and base (SS05). On September 24, 2014, a sub-surface investigation was completed to confirm attenuation of petroleum hydrocarbon impacts within the former excavation extent. Three boreholes (BH06-BH08) were advanced in the former locations of excavation soil samples SS03 - SS05, which exhibited constituent concentrations above regulatory standards. Soil samples were collected from BH06 at 20 feet bgs (previously SS05) and BH07 and BH08 at 12 feet bgs (previously SS04 and SS03, respectively). Analytical results indicated constituent concentrations were below regulatory standards in the three soil sample locations. Borehole locations and former excavation soil sample locations are illustrated on Figure 3. Soil analytical data is summarized in Table 1, laboratory analytical reports are included as Attachment A, and boring logs are included as Attachment B.
Additional Spill Details: Based on the soil analytical data provided herein, no remaining hydrocarbon impacts above regulatory standards are present in the area of soil samples SS03 - SS05. Consequently, PDC is requesting a produced water vault closure and a No Further Action (NFA) determination for this release.
Root Cause: A historic release was discovered below the produced water vessel during plug and abandonment activities.
Preventative Measures: The production facility was not rebuilt.

Lease Operator noticed bubbles emanating from a rain water puddle on location after servicing a tank vapor line. Initial investigation revealed gas was escaping from a 1inch line that is used periodically to pressure up a vapor line that runs from the tanks to the ECB to blow trapped fluid back into tank knock out pot. Gas pressure for this procedure is less than 40 pounds. Once Lease Operator relieved the trapped pressure on the 1 inch line the gas release stopped. Excavation of line revealed a corroded fitting on the line was allowing gas and fluid to be released when the line was pressured up. Staining was noted in the soil and the determination was made to remove the suspected contaminated soil. Based upon volumn of the soil removed (approiximately 15 yards) on 5/21/15 determination was made that release was more likely more than 1 BBL.
Area Depth Determined: Measurement of excavation.
Root Cause: Corrosion on fitting of 1 inch steel line caused line to fail allowing gas and fluid to escape when line was pressured up.  Line was used to provide pressure to blow trapped fluids from vapor line back into tank knock out pot.
Preventative Measures: Ensure all below grade steel lines are properly wrapped and protected to prevent corrosion.

Municipality: On the edge of the city limits of Greeley,CO
Spill Description: At just below ground level, ~6 feet from the oil and gas separator inlet, a 2" 3000# flanged valve parted at the flange rupturing the flowline, and exposing the release of gas lifted production vertically to the atmosphere.  During four flow "events" (one/day across four days), each lasting approximately 5 minutes, the well released, based on production averages from this well, a total of approximately 1 and 1/2 bbls of total fluid (hydrocarbons and production water).  A portion of the fluid from these releases settled on the graveled surface immediately around the point of rupture.  The remainder, atomized by the gas pressure, was carried by wind of variable direction and velocity into the corn field immediately adjacent to this production facility.  Upon discovery, Monday afternoon, August 31, the well was shut-in for repair.  There had been no pooling of fluid at the site, and so no fluid was recoverable.
Area Depth Determined: Visual inspection, test potholing of the facility area immediately around the point of rupture; subsequent sampling, and preliminary analyses performed by CGRS, who have informed us that the soil in the cornfield was not impacted.
Geology Description: High clay content topsoil over ancient river bed alluvium.

Spill Description: On Monday October 12th, 2015 DCP Midsteam operations discovered a condensate spray spill at our Rocky Compressor Station. It was determined that on Sunday October 11th, 2015 the liquid level in the TEG Afterscrubber reached a high-high level and opened a safety control valve to the TEG Flash Tank. The volume and pressure of liquid being routed to the TEG Flash Tank quickly over pressurized the TEG Flash Tank and a safety control valve was opened to a knockout-pot with atmosphere vent.  As the high pressure liquid was sent to the knockout pot it was then routed to the atmosphere as a fine-mist spray that traveled to the north of the facility. As the mist traveled to the north it settled on facility equipment and the ground; including rock, soil, and vegetation. Clean-up of the spill incident is ongoing and more information will be included in the 10-day follow-up report.

Spill Description: On Monday October 12th, 2015 DCP Midsteam operations discovered a condensate spray spill at our Rocky Compressor Station. It was determined that on Sunday October 11th, 2015 the liquid level in the TEG Afterscrubber reached a high-high level and opened a safety control valve to the TEG Flash Tank. The volume and pressure of liquid being routed to the TEG Flash Tank quickly over pressurized the TEG Flash Tank and a safety control valve was opened to a knockout-pot with atmosphere vent.  As the high pressure liquid was sent to the knockout pot it was then routed to the atmosphere as a fine-mist spray that traveled to the north of the facility. As the mist traveled to the north it settled on facility equipment and the ground; including rock, soil, and vegetation. Clean-up of the spill incident is ongoing and more information will be included in the 10-day follow-up report.
Root Cause: Liquid level in the TEG Afterscrubber reached a high-high level and opened a safety control valve to the TEG Flash Tank. The volume and pressure of liquid being routed to the TEG Flash Tank quickly over pressurized the TEG Flash Tank and a safety control valve was opened to a knockout-pot with atmosphere vent.  As the high pressure liquid was sent to the knockout pot it was then routed to the atmosphere as a fine-mist spray that traveled to the north of the facility.
Preventative Measures: DCP Operations and Engineering added a control valve downstream of the TEG after scrubber. The installed valve can be automatically closed in the cause of two scenarios; 1, low liquid level in the scrubber or 2, high-pressure in TEG flash tank. If either of these scenarios occurs the valve will close preventing flow to the TEG flash tank. In the case of this spill incident, scenario 2 was the root cause of the spill, adding the valve will prevent this type of spill from reoccurring.

Geology Description: The USGS Soil Survey Regional map indicates that the site surface soils are characterized as Aridisols and the nearby offsite soils to the west and south are characterized as Moolisols.  The overexcavation activities have encountered native uniform fine to medium silty/ clayey sand.  According to the USGS Regional Geologic Map #I-856-H the surface geology is characterized by unconsoldiated Quaternary Colluvium materials which are underlain by the Cretaceous Arapahoe Formation.  The Arapahoe arkosic sandstone bedrock was encountered at approximately 14 feet BGL.  The USGS Regional Depth to Water Table Map #I-856-K indicates that the depth to groundwater is typically more than 20 feet BGL and commonly greater than 100 feet BGL.  Groundwater has not been encoutnered in the excavation.
Additional Spill Details: Over-excavation activities to the west may be restricted due to the close proximity of the north-south trending Suncor -High Pressure Oil Pipe Line.  Suncor represnetatives verbally indicated that they did not encounter any subsurface impacts while installing the pipelien, down to an approximate depth of 8 feet BGL.  The above reference to the nearest water well, is a monitoring well installed by RTD.  According to the Colorado DNR the available water well permit records indicate that four (4) monitoring wells (MWs) were reportedly installed between the railroad tracks and the access road from 144th south approx 1/4 mile.  Monitoring well permit # 284940 was the closest well to the subject tank battery.  The wells were installed to depths of 15 or 25 feet BGL.  No groundwater depths were reported in the well files.  MEC Inc. has not observed any visible surface features for these MWs.  The nearby surface water features (ponds/streams) are illustrated intermittent (seasonal) water features.  Wetland type vegetation was observed along the drainage located approx 3500 feet east of the site.    Additional information Inlcuded as Attachments:   Form 27 ,  Site Aerial Photograph location map,  and tank battery site schematic.

Root Cause: A valve was left in the open position during routine maintenance at the 101 check meter valve. Spill Description: Equipment failure being the cause of the spill.  NGL stopped the flow of water to the facility as well as through the damaged equipment.  NGL used vacuum truck to pull all the water - both rainwater and spilled production water (390 bbls) - from the emergency pit and then made appropriate equipment repairs.    A spill retention pond exists on the south side of the location. The pond worked as designed, directing all of the water oto the pond which retained product until removal.   Contamination was determined by checking the product's SDS, measuring the exposed area, and counting the BBLs removed from the emergency pit.    Soil sampling was completed to determine the level of contamination. Then there was removal of all contaminated product to an appropriate disposal site.   NGL has since replaced all gaskets, and lowered the relief valve pressure settings.
Root Cause: Two events occurred that caused the spill of 400 bbls of water on 9/26/2017.  First, digital communication between NGL's Apollo facility and NGL's C7 facility failed. As an overview, when the Apollo facility reaches a high tank level, a motor-operated valve closes to prevent the tank from overfilling. Simultaneously, the Apollo site communicates with the C7 site to shut off the pump, which directs water to Apollo.  However, the communication between the two facilites failed due to a bad internet signal.  This caused the pipeline to pressure up, and finally a high-pressure set point at th C7 location ultimately shut down the pipeline. Secondly, a buna gasket failed between the time the motor-operated valve closed at Apollo and the pump shutting down from the high pressure at the C7 location.   Root Causes being both the communication between the facilities being lost due to a bad signal, and the gasket blowing out due to high pressure.
Preventative Measures: NGL has since installed a 20 foot antenna at the Apollo location to ensure a much more consistent connnection between the facilities.  We have also programmed in a communication loss shutdown.  If the Apollo and C7 sites lose communication for 5 minutes or more, the pipelines will now shut down.    NGL has also replaced all buna gaskets with spiral flex gaskets to prevent the gaskets from failing down the road.  Additionally, NGL has reduced the high pressure shut down on the pipeline from 150 psi to 130 psi, also reducing the pressure relief valve at the Apollo facility to 100 psi.

Spill Description: On Tuesday, September 12th, 2017 at approximately 11:45 AM, lighting struck the tank battery on the C19 596 well pad on Garden gulch Mesa in Garfield County, CO. The lightning strike and resulting fire were witnessed by Berry Petroleum Company operator Vinny Taylor as he was approaching the pad. The strike threw one 300 bbl tank approximately 150 yards off location, blew apart a second 300 bbl tank and destroyed a third 300 bbl tank. The single well on location was not producing at the time of the strike as it had been shut in since September 7th, 2017. Production superintendent Derek Johnson arrived on site at approximately 12:40 PM to oversee the incident response. A wide and thorough inspection of the surrounding land found no signs of a hyrocarbon spill on or in the soil. At this time it is believed all hydrocarbons in the tanks were consumed in the fires following the lightning strike.
Area Depth Determined: Measuring excavated area that was stained and/or odorous.
Root Cause: Lightning struck production tanks causing an explosion and resulting fire which burned most of oil and/or condensate that was in the three 300 bbl tanks.  All three tanks were destroyed and replaced.
Preventative Measures: Berry is investigating installation of a lightning elimination system.

Spill Description: Suspected soil contamination upon removal of produced water storage tank. Site has been shut in since 5/22/2017. On 9/14/2017, CGRS screened soil using a PID. The most impacted soil was found on the surface or within 6” of the surface of the excavation, directly between the edge of the produced water tank and the oil tanks.  The impacts decreased slightly at 1’ bgs, but drastically by 2’ bgs.  Trace hydrocarbon concentrations were still found at 4’ bgs. One soil sample was retained for laboratory analysis. Impacted soil will be removed and properly disposed of.
Area Depth Determined: A PID was used to identify impacted soil and direct excavation activities. Five confirmation soil samples to were collected between October 5-11, 2017, from below the previous location of the produced water tank, and the north, south, east, and west walls of the excavation. Soil samples were submitted to Origins Laboratory from analysis of BTEX, TEPH, and TVPH. Laboratory results indicate petroleum constituents were below laboratory MDLs in all five sample locations.
Geology Description: The soil profile at North Poudre consists of loosely compacted, poorly-sorted gravely sand to 3 feet bgs, where it transitions to well compacted, well-sorted silty sand.
Root Cause: Upon moving the oil storage tanks outside the soil secondary containment berm, surficial staining was observed below the west oil storage tank to a depth of 3 feet bgs. A 3" abandoned steel dumpline, trending east-to-west, was discovered under the oil tanks at approximately 6 feet bgs, and appeared to be another source of contamination.
Preventative Measures: The North Poudre facility has been shut-in. All existing process and storage equipment has been removed from the location.

Spill Description: On November 20, 2017, saturated soils were observed around the produced water sump during a routine inspection at the HSR-Shutt Federal 1-18A and 8-18A production facility. The release occurred when the produced water dump fitting connected to the produced water sump failed due to tank settling, allowing produced water to be released inside secondary containment. The release became State reportable on December 7, 2017, due to the quantity of impacted soil excavated. A topographic Site Location Map showing the geographic setting of the release is provided as Figure 1.
Area Depth Determined: On November 20, 2017, saturated soils were observed around the produced water sump during a routine inspection at the HSR-Shutt Federal 1-18A and 8-18A production facility. Approximately 300 cubic yards of impacted material were removed and transported to the Kerr-McGee land treatment facility in Weld County, Colorado. Nine (9) confirmation soil samples were collected from the sidewalls and base of the final extent of the excavation area at approximately 5 feet and 6 feet below ground surface (bgs), respectively. One (1) additional confirmation soil sample was collected from the ground surface west of the excavation area, which displayed saturated soil conditions outside of secondary containment. The soil samples were submitted to Origins Laboratory for analysis of benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, total xylenes (BTEX), total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) - gasoline range organics (GRO) by USEPA Method 8260C, TPH - diesel and oil range organics (DRO and ORO) by USEPA Method 8015, electrical conductivity (EC), and pH. Soil analytical results indicated that constituent concentrations in the soil samples collected from the sidewalls and base of the final extent of the excavation area and the observed saturated soil area outside of secondary containment were below the applicable COGCC Table 910-1 standards. A topographic Site Location Map showing the geographic setting of the release is provided as Figure 1. Soil sample locations are illustrated on Figure 2. Soil analytical results are summarized in Table 1 and the laboratory analytical reports are provided as Attachment A.
Root Cause: A release occurred when the produced water dump fitting connected to the produced water sump failed due to tank settling, allowing produced water to be released inside secondary containment.
Preventative Measures: The production facility will be rebuilt.

Other Waste: Small amount of oil sprayed out of the top of a tank.  Mixed with snowmelt in containment.
Spill Description: Small amount of oil spilt from tanks but contained within the secondary containment. The tank was around 90% capacity and a high pressure two phase on the vessel had a dump frozen open.  High pressure gas was sent into the tank PRV failed or was overloaded and the gas injected caused oil to spray out of the top of tank.  Oil sprayed out was kept within the containment, snowmelt combined with the oil inside the containment.  Some pea gravel was removed and placed in a temporary containment, the pea gravel discharged some oil and combined water from snow.  This fluid has already been removed and the pea gravel has been replaced.  The problem was kept within containment.
Area Depth Determined: Soil around the tank containment was visually inspected for any oil.  There was no oil present outside of containment.
Geology Description: Pea gravel within our containment was the only contaminated material.
Root Cause: The root cause of the incident would be the freezing of the dump valve that caused the gas to enter the tank.  The PRV on the tank also failed and released causing oil to spray out of the tank when the tank was not overloaded requiring a pressure release.
Preventative Measures: We will be re-evaluating insulation and heat trace placement to prevent the freeze from happening again.  PRV has been inspected and repaired.  We have talked with all pumpers involved in the incident and discussed their view of the accident and the cause.  We will increase our inspection frequency on tank valves.

Spill Description: DCP Environmental was informed by DCP Pipeline group of a possible pipeline release on January 17th, 2018 around 2:00 pm. At the time of notification the DCP pipeline group had identified that a 2 inch gas gathering pipeline valve downstream of a meter has frozen. When the valve froze water and a small amount of hydrocarbons were released from the pipeline. There was no visible staining on the surface to indicate soil contamination; however, standing liquid was present around the meter and above piping. The pipeline has been isolated and blowdown, and until repairs have been made the pipeline will remain out of service. DCP Field Operations repaired the valve on January 18th, 2018. A DCP Environmental Group representative as well as a third party contractor will be conducting site investigation during the week of January 22nd, 2018 to determine the extent of soil contamination and develop a remediation plan as needed.
Area Depth Determined: Onsite observation of soil characteristics and screening with photoionization detector (PID). Soil samples were collected and submitted for labratory analysis.

Spill Description: DCP Environmental was informed by DCP Pipeline group of a possible pipeline release on January 17th, 2018 around 2:00 pm. At the time of notification the DCP pipeline group had identified that a 6 inch gas gathering pig launcher had froze. When the launcher froze water and a small amount of hydrocarbons were released from the pipeline. There was no visible staining on the surface to indicate soil contamination; however, standing liquid was present. The launcher and associated pipeline had been out of service, and will remain so unless otherwise determined. A DCP Environmental Group representative as well as a third party contractor will be conducting site investigation during the week of February 5th, 2018 to determine the extent of soil contamination and develop a remediation plan as needed.
Area Depth Determined: The extent was determined during the initial investigation by hand auger bore holes starting near the launcher to approximately 40 feet. Five sample locations were investigated with samples collected at 6 inch intervals for onsite analysis with a photoionization detector (PID) and 2 soil samples submitted for lab analysis. At this time the lab analysis has not been returned, so true extent of soil contamination is unknown.

Spill Description: DCP Environmental was informed by DCP Pipeline group of a possible pipeline release on January 17th, 2018 around 2:00 pm. These data were used to guide subsequent excavation activities and delineate impacted surface soil material. Three (3) soil samples were collected from the base of the shallow excavation area as illustrated in the attached Figure 1. The sample with the highest PID value was submitted to the laboratory for analysis of BTEX, TPH-GRO and TPH-DRO. Sample results were reported below applicable COGCC standards. Additional detail provided in the attached summary report and NFA Request.
Geology Description: Silty sands and gravel - non-native road base and fill material

Preventative Measures: The pipeline was repaired by DCP Field Operations on January 18th, 2018.

Spill Description: DCP Environmental was informed by DCP Pipeline group of a pipeline release on May 4, 2018 around 8:00 am. The DCP pipeline group identified a leaking valve associated with an above ground 4 inch gas gathering pipeline. A small amount of water and hydrocarbons were released form the pipeline, which resulted in an area of visible stained soils. However, at the time it did not appear the spill was large enough to consider reporting. The  pipeline and meter house was isolated, blowndown, and infrastructure removed. At the time of equipment and soil removal, the impacted area was discovered to be larger than anticipated and subsequently reportable. On June 18 and 19, 2018, additional excavation activities were performed by Tasman to remove remaining impacted soils from the site. Based on completed remedial activities, DCP is requesting a no further action (NFA) determination fot the site. Supporting documentation is attached.
Area Depth Determined: During excavation activities, surrounding soils were field screened with a photoionization detector (PID) and standard headspace soil sampling techniques. These data were used to guide subsequent excavation activities and delineate impacted soil material. Six (6) perimeter soil samples were collected from the sidewalls and base of the excavation at the locations illustrated on the attached Figure 2 and retained for laboratory analysis. Based on laboratory analytical results, BTEX, TPH-DRO and TPH-GRO concentrations were reported below applicable COGCC soil standards and confirm that petroleum hydrocarbon impacts were successfully removed from the Site through excavation activities. Additional details are provided in the attached Form 19 Summary Letter and NFA Recommendation.
Geology Description: Aquolls and Aquents, gravelly substratum. Silty sand, course.
Root Cause: A small leak was identified in a valve assembly associated with an above ground portion of a DCP 4-inch pipeline. A small amount of water and hydrocarbons were released from the leak resulting in localized soil impacts.
Preventative Measures: The associated pipeline has been blowndown, removed from service and capped. Above ground piping and infrastructure has been removed.

Spill Description: DCP Environmental was informed by DCP Pipeline group of a possible pipeline release on January 29th, 2018 around 8:00 am. At the time of notification the DCP pipeline group had identified that a 6 inch gas gathering pipeline valve had been inadvertently opened. When the valve opened water and a small amount of hydrocarbons were released from the pipeline. There was no visible staining on the surface to indicate soil contamination; however, standing liquid was present. The valve has been closed and the associated pipeline has been isolated and blowdown, and will remain out of service. A DCP Environmental Group representative as well as a third party contractor will be conducting site investigation during the week of February 5th, 2018 to determine the extent of soil contamination and develop a remediation plan as needed.
Area Depth Determined: Based on initial field observations from January 28, 2018 soil impacts appeared localized to a small pooled area of water and petroleum hydrocarbons in close proximity to the point of release. No visible staining was observed beyond the area of pooled liquid and the total volume of fluids released to the ground surface were estimated to be less than one (1) barrel (bbl) and not large enought to be considered a reportable incident. However, to fully delineate impacts to soil and verify soil concentrations, on February 9, 2018 hand augur soil sampling activities were conducted at the Site and a total of seven (7) soil samples were collected and submitted to Summit Scientific Laboratories (Summit) in Golden, CO for laboratory analysis of BTEX and TPH-GRO/DRO. Two (2) of the submitted samples were returned with constituents of concern (COC) concentrations above COGCC Table 910-1 standards. On August 1, 2018 subsequent to removal of all above and below ground piping, structures, and ancillary equipment associated with the meter houses, impacted soil excavation and disposal activities were performed. A total of approximately 25 cubic yards of impacted soil was removed and transported under waste manifesting procedures to the North Weld Waste Management Landfill in Ault, CO for disposal. Five (5) perimeter soil samples were collected from the extents of the excavation and submitted to Summit for laboratory analysis of BTEX and TPH-GRO/DRO. Based on the laboratory analytical results, COC concentrations at all 5 sampled locations were reported below laboratory detection limits and the COGCC soil standards indicating that petroleum hydrocarbon impacts to soil at the Site were mitigated. Therefore, a no further action (NFA) determination is being requested for the Site. Please refer to the attached Form 19 Supplemental Summary Letter and NFA Request for detailed information regarding the field activities described above.
Additional Spill Details: Please refer to the attached Form 19 Supplemental Summary Letter and NFA Request for additional information.
Root Cause: A valve on a 6-inch gas gathering line at a meter house location on-Site had been inadvertently opened for unkown reasons. The pipeline was subsequently isolated, blown down and is out of service. All ancillary equipemnt on-Site that was associated with the pipeline has been removed and the line was cut and capped below grade.
Preventative Measures: All equipment has been removed from the location, the gathering line is out of service, and the pipeline was cut and capped below grade.

Spill Description: DCP Environmental was informed by DCP Pipeline group of a possible pipeline release on January 21, 2019. At the time of notification, the DCP pipeline group had determined that a 3-inch gas gathering pipeline had developed a leak. The pipeline was isolated and blown down and placed out of service until further investigation and repairs could be performed. On January 23, 2019, a third-party contractor exposed the pipeline and identified a small hole at the 7-O’clock position, which was determined to be caused by external corrosion. On January 23 and 25, 2019, a third-party environmental remediation contractor provided oversight for remediation of soils impacted by the pipeline release. Subsequently, the pipeline leak was repaired by removing a 3-foot section of pipe where the leak occurred, and a new section of pipe was welded in place. The pipeline was inspected, wrapped with corrosion preventative tape prior to backfilling and pressure tested prior to being placed back in service.
Area Depth Determined: On January 23 and 25, 2019, soil investigation activities were performed to delineate the extent of soil impacts as a result of the pipeline release. Excavated soils and sidewalls were field screened utilizing a photoionization detector (PID) and standard headspace field screening  methods. Soil impacts in the vicinity of the release were observed to extend primarily from 3-feet to 10-feet below ground surface (bgs). Soils samples collected from the initial excavation extents on January 23, 2019 were submitted for laboratory analysis of benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, total xylenes, (BTEX), and total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) gasoline range organics (GRO) using United States Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) Method 8260B and TPH diesel range organics (DRO) using USEPA Method 8015. Soil sample analytical results were confirmed to have petroleum hydrocarbon impacts above the COGCC Table 910-1 standards indicating that further remediation activities were required. Due to inclement weather on January 24, 2019, supplemental delineation and remediation activities were postponed. Further excavation and soil delineation activities were conducted on January 25, 2019 and confirmation samples, collected from the excavation sidewalls and base, were submitted for laboratory analysis of BTEX and TPH-GRO/DRO using the USEPA Methods described above. Soil sample analytical results were confirmed to be below COGCC standards indicating all impacted soils were successfully removed during remediation activities. Approximately 190 cubic yards (CY) were removed from the excavation and transported for off-site disposal at the Waste Management - Buffalo Ridge Landfill facility. The attached Figures 1 and 2 illustrate the site location, extent of excavation, confirmation sample locations, and associated confirmation soil sample analytical results. The attached Table 1 provides a summary of analytical results and the laboratory analytical report is also provided for reference.
Geology Description: Organic soils with fine and silty sands from approximately 0 to 5 feet bgs, weathered clay from approximatley 5 to 9 feet bgs, and consolidated clay at 10 feet bgs. Olney loamy sand, 1 to 3 percent slopes.
Additional Spill Details: During excavation activities, a relatively small volume of water was observed to infiltrate the excavation through parts of the sidewall as the soil transitioned from fine and silty sand to weathered clay at approximately 5 feet below ground surface (bgs). However, the inflow of water was intermittent, was not observed throughout the excavation, dry soils were observed below areas with infiltrating water, and the flow of water stopped after the sidewalls were left open for a short period of time. Therefore, the observed water is considered perched water and unrelated to a groundwater table beneath the Site. Additionally, nearby water well records were consulted and indicate that the shallow groundwater bearing zone in the area is encountered at approximately 28 feet bgs. Infiltrated water was mixed with excavated soil and removed for disposal at the landfill.
Root Cause: A 3-inch gas gathering pipeline developed a small hole as a result of external corrosion of the steel pipe located at the 7'Oclock position on the pipe. The hole leaked an unkown volume of condensate material into the surrounding subsurface soils which eventually surfaced and was identified on January 21, 2019.
Preventative Measures: A 3-foot section of pipeline was removed and a new section of pipe was welded in place. The repaired section of pipeline was inspected, integrity tested, coated with corrosion resistant wrapping, and pressure tested prior to backfilling and the line being placed back into service.

Approximately 890 cubic yards of impacted soil were excavated and transported to Buffalo Ridge Landfill in Keenesburg, Colorado, for disposal. The general site layout, excavation dimensions, and soil sample locations are depicted on the Excavation Site Map provided as Figure 2. The soil sample analytical results are summarized in Table 1, and the laboratory analytical reports are attached.
Additional Spill Details: No further action is required. Laboratory analytical results for the soil samples indicated that TPH and BTEX concentrations were in full compliance with COGCC Table 910-1 allowable levels at the extent of the excavation. Based on the soil sample analytical results, Kerr-McGee is requesting a No Further Action status for this site. The original Form 19 NFA Status Request, submitted to the COGCC on May 16, 2013, is included as an attachment.
Root Cause: On May 10, 2013, a corrosion hole on the 53-4” pipeline resulted in the release of oil and produced water to the subsurface. The volume of the release is unknown.
Preventative Measures: The corroded portion of the pipeline was replaced and cathodic protection was installed.

An internally leaking valve was discovered during a routine inspection at the 16-18-1453-4 Launcher location. The leaked condensate overfilled a small containment, resulting in a release of less than 1 barrel outside of secondary containment.  Approximately 360 barrels (75 cubic yards) of impacted material were removed via hydro-vaccum and transported to the Kerr-McGee Aggregate Recycle Facility in Weld County, Colorado. Excavation activities were guided in the field by screening soil for volatile organic compound (VOC) concentrations using a photoionization detector (PID). Groundwater was encountered within the excavation at approximately 15 feet below ground surface (bgs). Approximately 60 barrels of groundwater were removed from the excavation via vacuum truck and transported to the Kerr-McGee Aggregate Recycle Facility. A topographic Site Location Map showing the geographic setting of the release is provided as Figure 1.
Area Depth Determined: An internally leaking valve was discovered during a routine inspection at the 16-18-1453-4 Launcher location. Eight (8) confirmation soil samples were collected from the sidewalls and base of the final extent of the excavation area at depths ranging from approximately 2 feet to 15 feet bgs. The soil samples were submitted to Origins Laboratory for analysis of benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, total xylenes (BTEX), napthalene, total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) - gasoline range organics (GRO) by USEPA Method 8260C, TPH - diesel and oil range organics (DRO and ORO) by USEPA Method 8015. Laboratory analytical results indicated that constituent concentrations in the soil samples collected from the final extent of the excavation area were in full compliance with the COGCC standards. Groundwater was encountered in the excavation at approximately 15 feet bgs. On July 12, 2019, one groundwater sample (GW01) was collected from the excavation and submitted to Origins Laboratory for analysis of BTEX by USEPA Method 8260C. Analytical results received on July 15, 2019, indicated that the benzene, toluene, and total xylenes concentrations in groundwater sample GW01 were out of compliance with the COGCC standards. Prior to backfilling, approximately 60 barrels of groundwater were removed from the excavation via vacuum truck, and approximately 55 pounds of activated carbon were introduced into the excavation to address residual impacts to groundwater. The phreatic zone was backfilled with clean sand and the excavation area was graded to match pre-existing conditions.
Additional Spill Details: A topographic Site Location Map showing the geographic setting of the release is provided as Figure 1. Soil and groundwater sample locations are illustrated on Figure 2. Soil analytical results are summarized in Table 1 and groundwater analytical results are summarized in Table 2. The laboratory analytical reports are provided as Attachment A.  An Initial Form 27 Site Investigation and Remediation Workplan will be prepared for this release.
Root Cause: The release originated from an internally leaking 2-inch drain valve at a pipeline pig launching location. The leaked condensate overfilled a small containment, resulting in a release to the ground.
Preventative Measures: The affected valve will be replaced prior to the launching location being returned to service.

Spill Description: Produced water dump line failed, releasing approximatly 2 on barrels. Facility was shut in, and clean up scheduled.
Area Depth Determined: On June 18, 2019 Tasman completed a site assessment to determine potential soil and groundwater impacts associated with the dump line release at the Foster 3-35, 6-35, UPRR 53, Pan Am 2 tank battery. Seven boreholes were installed via hand auger.  Soil boring locations are illustrated on Figure 2, and boring logs are included in Attachment A. During soil boring activities, soil samples were collected and field screened for VOCs using a PID and standard head space sampling techniques. Soil samples from the depth interval exhibiting the highest PID reading above the groundwater table were retained for laboratory analysis. Seven soil samples were submitted to Summit Scientific Laboratory in Golden, Colorado (Summit) for laboratory analysis of benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, and total xylenes (BTEX), naphthalene, and total petroleum hydrocarbons-gasoline range organics (TPH-GRO) using United States Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) Method 8260B, as well as total petroleum hydrocarbons-diesel range organics (TPH-DRO) using USEPA Method 8015. Samples BH05@0-2’ and BH06@0-2’ was also analyzed for Sodium Adsorption Ratio (SAR) by USEPA Method 6020 / United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Method 60 6(2,3A) and Specific Conductance (EC) and pH via American Public Health Association (APHA)/American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM)/USEPA methods .  Soil analytical results are summarized in Table 1. Complete laboratory analytical reports are included in Attachment B. During the assessment, groundwater was encountered at approximately 12 ft below ground surface (bgs). One temporary monitoring well was installed (BH04) to evaluate potential dissolved phase impacts to groundwater. Temporary monitoring well, BH04, was developed and sampled using a dedicated, disposable, polyethylene bailer. The groundwater sample (BH04) was submitted to Summit for BTEX analysis using USEPA method 8260B.
Additional Spill Details: Laboratory analytical results for the soil samples collected in the area of the release the during Site assessment indicate that BTEX, naphthalene, TPH-GRO and TPH-DRO concentrations are below COGCC Table 910-1 soil standards. Laboratory results for the groundwater sample collected indicate that BTEX concentrations are below COGCC Table 910-1 groundwater standards.
Root Cause: Produced water dump line failed due to corrosion from inside out.
Preventative Measures: Facility has been decommissioned.

Spill Description: During decommissioning of a third party drilling fluid management facility, historical petroleum hydrocarbon impacts were encountered. The volume of the release is unknown and excavation activities are underway. The assessment details and analytical results will be summarized in a supplemental report. The topographic Site Location Map showing the geographic setting of the release is provided as Figure 1.
Area Depth Determined: On June 26, 2019, five 4-point composite soil samples and ten surface soil samples were collected from two existing soil piles and the onsite ditch. Between July 18 and 24, 2019, 30 soil samples were collected from the resulting excavation. The soil samples were submitted for laboratory analysis of TPH, BTEX, and naphthalene. The excavation base soil samples were also analyzed for pH, EC, and SAR. Laboratory analytical results indicate that TPH, BTEX, and naphthalene are in full compliance with COGCC Table 910-1 allowable levels for the composite soil pile samples. Laboratory analytical soil results indicate that TPH, BTEX, naphthalene, EC, and SAR concentrations and levels are in full compliance with COGCC Table 910-1 allowable levels at the extent of the excavation. Base soil sample B02@5’ exceeded the COGCC Table 910-1 allowable level for pH at 9.48 units. However, this sample was collected below the root zone (depth greater than 3 feet below ground surface); therefore, no further excavation was necessary. Approximately 720 cubic yards of petroleum hydrocarbon impacted soil were transported to Buffalo Ridge Landfill in Keenesburg, Colorado, for disposal. The general site layout, soil pile locations, excavation dimensions, and soil and groundwater sample locations are depicted on the Excavation Site Map provided as Figure 2. The soil and groundwater sample analytical results are summarized in Table 1 and Table 2, respectively. The laboratory analytical reports are attached.
Additional Spill Details: No further action is required. Laboratory analytical results for the soil samples indicate that TPH, BTEX, naphthalene, EC, and SAR concentrations and levels are in full compliance with COGCC Table 910-1 allowable levels at the extent of the excavation and in the two existing soil piles at the site. Laboratory analytical results indicated that sample B02@5’ exceeded the COGCC Table 910-1 allowable level for pH. However, this sample was collected below the root zone (depth greater than 3 feet below ground surface); therefore, no further excavation was necessary. Laboratory analytical results indicate that groundwater is in full compliance with COGCC Table 910-1 allowable levels. Based on the soil and groundwater sample analytical results, Kerr-McGee is requesting a No Further Action status for this site.
Root Cause: During decommissioning of a third-party drilling fluid management facility, historical petroleum hydrocarbon impacts were encountered. The volume of the release is unknown.
Preventative Measures: The third-party drilling fluid management facility is being decommissioned.

DCP Environmental was informed by DCP Pipeline group of a possible pipeline release on January 17th, 2018 around 2:00 pm. At the time of notification the DCP pipeline group had identified that a 6 inch gas gathering pig launcher had froze. When the launcher froze water and a small amount of hydrocarbons were released from the pipeline. There was no visible staining on the surface to indicate soil contamination; however, standing liquid was present. The launcher and associated pipeline had been out of service, and will remain so unless otherwise determined. A DCP Environmental Group representative as well as a third party contractor will be conducting site investigation during the week of February 5th, 2018 to determine the extent of soil contamination and develop a remediation plan as needed.
Area Depth Determined: On February 8, 2018, a Site investigation was conducted using hand augur drilling and soil sampling methods which were performed in the suspected source area near the pig launcher to approximately 40 feet downgradient. During investigation activities, recovered soils were field screened with a handheld photoionization detector (PID) and standard headspace soil sampling techniques to delineate areas of suspected soil impacts. Field investigation and soil sample analytical results are further described in the attached Form 19 Supplemental Summary Letter and NFA Request.
Geology Description: Silty sands with areas of inorganic clays. Regionally, wages fine sandy loam, 6 to 9 percent slopes.
Additional Spill Details: The Colorado Division of Water Resources Database was consulted for groundwater depth. The nearest registered water well recorded a static water depth of 70 feet bgs. The referenced depth was reported in this document. In accordance with the February 13, 2018 Form 19 I/S COA (Document #401544230), an explanation for the delay in release reporting is required. While a direct cause of the delay could not be identified, it is assumed that the delay was related to obtaining the correct contact information for the responsible party at the United States Forest Service, the landowner. Once the responsible party was identified, applicable notifications were completed.
Root Cause: An above ground 6-Inch gas gathering pig launcher froze and cracked due to cold temperatures. Residual water and hydrocarbons within the pipe were subsequently released from the pipeline when temperatures increased.
Preventative Measures: The launcher and associated pipeline have been shut-in and has remained out of service. Currently, there are no plans to place the associated  equipment back into service.

Area Depth Determined: The length is assumed to be the distance between the poly line break and the lower collection dam, the width is an approximation of the width of the gulch. Numerical values were determined via GIS.
Geology Description: The soils in the gulch are primarily unconsolidated sands, gravel, and clay.
Additional Spill Details: The water collected in the 12-inch poly was joining the impacted water from seeps located north (downstream) of the upper diversion roughly 500 feet south of the vault instead of in the sediment trap directly upstream of the vault. All water from the pipe as well as all water in the creek is still captured and treated to standards in Permit COG315481. Samples collected from the Spring and the Seep during third quarter 2019 had no detections of BTEX constituents above the laboratory reporting limits (see attached analytical report). See document 2573009 for a previously submitted timeline of repairs. The depth to groundwater is estimated based on data from the nearest monitoring well.
Root Cause: The 12-inch poly line collects and routes water from the southernmost spring to the lower dam where it joins the rest of the water from the creek. All water is captured at the lower dam and sent to the vault, then either pumped to the onsite water treatment plant or, if the plant is not operational, it is sent to an injection well for disposal. The poly line was discovered to have cracked and split approximately 500 feet from the lower dam, at a point where the ground surface drops substantially. It is believed the stress placed on the poly line from hanging off this ledge lead to material failure resulting in the break.
Preventative Measures: A new section of pipe was brought in to reconnect the line to the lower dam and bracing was installed to support the pipe in the area of the ledge. Repairs were completed October 25, 2019 and the pipe is currently back in service.

Spill Description: In July 2013, a leak was identified within a six-inch DCP gas gathering pipeline and resulted in a hydrocarbon release to soils at CR 20 and Highway (Hwy) 85 pipeline release (Site), located approximately 0.2 miles east on CR 20 from the intersection with Hwy 85, in Ft. Lupton, CO.  At the time of the release, the pipeline was isolated and blown down while repairs were completed. DCP contracted a third-party environmental contractor to delineate and remove impacted soils in the area of the release.  Analytical results from soil excavation and boring sample locations determined that soil impacts remained in place and required additional remediation. Beginning June 4, 2014 additional investigation activities were performed and included groundwater delineation activities, groundwater remediation and continued quarterly groundwater monitoring activities.
Area Depth Determined: During the July 2013 remediation efforts, approximately 400 cubic yard (CY) of impacted soils were removed by excavation methods and transported for off-site disposal. Confirmation soil samples were collected from the excavation sidewalls and base of excavation at locations illustrated on the attached Figure 2. Analytical results indicated soil impacts remained in place, however the extent of the excavation was limited at the time due to buried fiber optic utilities to the south and agricultural ditch to the north. Soil analytical data is provided in the attached Table 1 and analytical reports are also attached for reference. Additional soil boings were advanced and completed as monitoring wells to evaluate impacts to groundwater in June 2014. Between June 2014 and September 2015, six soil borings were advanced to approximately 18-feet bgs and completed as one-inch monitoring wells at locations illustrated on the attached Figure 3. Following monitoring well installation, ongoing groundwater monitoring has been performed at the Site on a quarterly basis through the third quarter 2019. Additionally, mobile vacuum enhanced fluid recovery (EFR) groundwater remediation efforts were conducted from the third quarter 2015 through the fourth quarter 2016 at which point light non-aqueous phase liquid (LNAPL) was no longer observed at the site. Historical soil excavation and boring analytical data is provided as an attachment to this submittal. Quarterly groundwater reports prepared from the second quarter 2015 through the third quarter 2019 will be provided as attachments in a subsequent eForm 27 submittal.

Sixteen (16) confirmation soil samples were collected from the sidewalls and bases of the final extents of the 2019 and 2020 wellhead excavation areas at depths ranging from approximately 7 to 15 feet below ground surface (bgs). The base soil samples were submitted for laboratory analysis of beznene, toluene, ethylbenzene, total xylenes (BTEX), naphthalene, and total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) - gasoline range organics (GRO) by United States Environmental Protection Agency (USEPA) Method 8260D, TPH - diesel range organics (DRO) and oil range organics (ORO) by USEPA Method 8015D, pH by USEPA Method 9045D, specific conductance (EC) by USEPA Method 9050A, and sodium adsorption ratio (SAR) by USDA Agricultural Handbook 60 Method 20B. Analytical results indicated that the soil samples collected from the final extents of the 2019 and 2020 wellhead excavation areas were in full compliance with the COGCC Table 910-1 standards. After additional investigation during the week of November 2nd, no additional flowline could be located, indicating the open ended flowline was responsible for the release. Preventative Measures: The open ended flowline has been blind flanged to prevent a future release form the release location. Check valves at the manifold were inspected and serviced. Flowline system will be pressure test in coordination with COGCC Engineering unit to confirm integrity of the system.

Spill Description: During the fall sampling of the groundwater monitoring wells at the P32 E&P waste facility a sample from MW-3 came back with high levels of methane. After an internal investigation for the Bunker Hill 094A Discharge point flume spill, it was determined that produced water from a combination of wells had overflowed the 12" constructed flume prior to the discharge point. The water was immediately re-routed through an installed gathering line, bypassing the flume infrastructure, and taking the water directly to the permitted discharge point.
GPS for the spill path are: 
Start 37.25267/-104.66744 End East 37.25258/-104.66732
Start 37.25267/-104.66744 End West 37.25211/-104.66762

It was determined that the Eastern flow path of the spill did infact reach state waters, solely made up of the CBM discharge water that ENR places on the ground. Between the east and west spill pathways, a total of 27.78 bbls of produced water were determined to have been released. The CDPHE Spill Report number for this release is 2021-0568. To prevent this type of incident happening at this location, and others where flumes are already, or plan to be installed, the minimum flume size standard has been increased from a 12" diameter to a 24" diameter. This will help with effective displacement of the produced water through the flume. Additionally, when cleaning the flumes, a more effective displacement of the river rock in the flumes has been discussed to additionally contain water that travels through the flume. In the mean time, the water at the Bunker Hill 094A discharge point is still going through the installed pipe, bypassing the flume altogether, until a larger 24" structure can be installed at the site.
Additional Spill Details: The water released from this spill was all CBM produced water that typically is discharged to state waters, in accordance with CDPHE permit CO0047767. The water quality is consistently within the CDPHE WQCD limits for this discharge point.
Root Cause: Root cause of the incident was determined to be the size of the flume, and the volume of produced water travelling through the flume. Additionally, the positioning of the river rocks in the flume led internal sources to believe that the high water volumes through the flume had contributed to the movement of the rocks, making the flume more susceptible to overflow.
Preventative Measures: The water at the discharge point was redirected to bypass the Flume until a larger flume can be installed at the discharge point. Going forward, only 24" flumes will be installed at large discharge points to prevent this from happening.

Spill Description:
Notified on Friday afternoon (4/15/2022) about a flowline failure by Jim Byers with the BLM.  The well was shut in and secured that afternoon.  Assessment and cleanup activities began on Monday 4/18/2022.  The flowline was repaired and excavated around the production tank and the well was returned to service.  Cause of release was pulled threads on flowline collar likely due freeze conditions.
Update 4/29/2022 - hydrocarbon stained soils were hand excavated and transported to Greenleaf for disposal.  Subsequent assessment activities will be scheduled once production tank can be emptied.
Area Depth Determined: Field measured and visually determined.  True depth of impact will be determined once production tank is moved and assessment activities begin.
Geology Description: Wrayha-Rabbites-Veatch complex, 45 to 65 percent slopes, very stony with sand
Root Cause: Flowline collar separated at threads likely due to freeze.
Preventative Measures: Collar replaced with new union rated to 2000 psi.  More frequent inspections will be conducted on area locations.

This is a split estate in the Cache Unit - Cache Unit (OWP) #26 is on fee land. Following a conversation with the surface owner on 4/26, the former pumper shut a valve on the wellhead, stopping the leak which was controlled within 30 minutes of discovery. The spill that traveled 50 ft SE stopped ~30 ft from a larger channel that conveys substantial annual stormwater. There is oil at the surface with affected vegetation, clear evidence of infiltration, and high potential to impact waterways.

Spill Description: At 6pm, on June 1, BLM agents discovered a drip on location of the Baldy Creek 2-20 and notified Jim Graves (Vision Energy pumper). First thing on June 2, 2022, Jim traveled to location, closed the valve causing the drip. He determined that a wild animal (likely a bear) broke the barrier surrounding the well head and rubbed on the equipment, opening the valve that caused the leak.  In short: valve was closed and replaced by a plug, all parties agreed no water was impacted, Baldy Creek was in no way affected, no produced water left the location and only a 10'x10' area was affected by the spill. Vision understood that the volume was less than 1 bbl before the 24 hour expiration. Notification was still completed because of proximity to waters of Colorado. Soil sampling was completed - test results are delayed due to COVID.  Attached is a comprehensive description of the incident as first reported via email to both COGCC and BLM on June 2, 2022.

Spill Description: A pin sized hole in a crude oil storage tank resulted in a release within secondary containment. KPK shut-in the well on March 23, 2022 and drained the tank to stop any further contamination. A hydrovac and traditional excavation equipment were used by KPK to remove surface impacts. All contaminated material was properly disposed of off-site.
Area Depth Determined: Extent of impacts were determined utilizing excavation, extent of impacts have not been fully delineated at this point, calculated volume were based off of visual surface impacts at the site, during the time of discovery.
Additional Spill Details: Fifty-two (52) tons of impacted soil were removed and disposed of from this location. Waste Disposal Manifest reflects total weight of saturated material removed via hydrovac and combined with woodchips and traditionally excavated material.
Root Cause: The release occurred due to a small pin hole caused by internal corrosion of the Tank. KPK operators immediately dispatched a Hydro-Vac crew to the site to plug the hole, and to remove all remaining product free the tank, and all free surface product to eliminate migration from the site.
Preventative Measures: Facility integrity testing schedules are being implemented to decrease the potential of future releases, the tank has been plugged and patched and will be replaced, under a Form 27.

A topographic Site Location Map showing the geographic setting of the release is provided as Figure 1. The soil sample location is illustrated on Figure 2. Soil sample location and field screening data are provided in Table 1. Soil sample analytical results are summarized in Tables 2 through 5. The laboratory analytical report is provided as Attachment A. Field notes and a photographic log are provided as Attachment B. The State Notification email is provided as Attachment C.

The release occurred due to excessive rain causing a partially buried tank to be submerged, resulting in fluids coming out of the
tank.

This form is to notify you of a State Reportable Release of an unknown volume of gas and fluid on a WES DJ Gathering LLC (f/k/a Kerr- McGee Gathering, LLC, COGCC Operator ID: 47121) location impacting a single residence. WES is not aware of any impact to Waters of the State, Public Water Systems, livestock, wildlife, air quality, or publicly-maintained roads. The line has been shut-in to contain the release and the release is being investigated. 

Assessment activities are ongoing and will be tied into a Form 27 remediation report.
Area Depth Determined: Between July 26, 2023, and August 3, 2023, a total of 57 soil samples were collected from in and around the excavation, two swab samples from the residence, two crawlspace surface water samples, one indoor air sample from the residence, and seven soil vapor samples from around the excavation of the residence. The soil samples were field screened for volatile organic compounds using a photoionization detector (PID) and the indoor air sample locations were field screened using a GEM 5000 methane meter prior to sample collection. All soil samples and crawl space water samples were submitted for analysis in accordance with COGCC rule 913.h. The indoor air samples and vapor point samples were submitted for analysis for full list of VOCs per EPA Method TO-15. The impacted soil was excavated to the maximum extent allowable due to site conditions. Based on soil analytical results, additional excavation is needed west of the potential release location. The PID readings, soil, air and surface water sample results are summarized in table, 1,2,3,4,5 and 6, respectively, and laboratory reports attached in Document Number 403525725, dated 09/14/2023.

Spill Description: During a site inspection conducted by an ECMC representative, some minor spills and leaks were noted around production equipment areas, specifically at the treater (injection pump) and near vessels. Upon initial inspection all spills have remained on the tank battery location and have remained immediately adjacent to equipment. Cleanup and equipment evaluation and repair activities will begin as soon as possible.
Area Depth Determined: Visual and olfactory impacted soil could be seen around the injection pump (formerly referred to as the "treater"). This material was hand dug out and was replaced with clean soil to assist with observing any potential leaks from the pump in the future. The injection pump is scheduled to be serviced at the end of this month, and the stained area shall be cleaned out while the pump is out of service. Additional soil removal and soil sampling per Table 915 requirements shall be completed and reported on a subsequent Supplemental Form 19
Additional Spill Details: Various locations of asphaltic oil on the ground surface were also cleaned out and removed from the wellhead, tank load-out areas, around the injection pump building, and around the produced water pits.
Root Cause: Oil sump pump failed and did not empty the sump fast enough causing lubricant oil to overtop the sump.
Preventative Measures: The sump pump has been replaced. Additional servicing of the injection pump is scheduled to be conducted to help reduce the build up of oil in the sump.

Spill Description: On March 28, 2024, historically impacted soil was discovered following cut and cap and wellhead flowline riser removal activities at the Inouye 11-31A wellhead location. Excavation and assessment activities are ongoing. A topographic Site Location Map showing the geographic setting of the release is provided as Figure 1.
Area Depth Determined: Following cut and cap and flowline removal operations at the Inouye 11-31A wellhead location on February 12 and 14, 2024, soil samples were collected from the base of the wellhead excavation area (WH-B01@6'), from the locations where the flowline risers were disconnected at the wellhead (FL-B01@4') and separator (FL-B09@4'), and where the flowline changed direction (FL-B03@4' and FL-B08@4'). The soil samples were submitted for laboratory analysis of the full Table 915-1 analytical suite, using standard methods appropriate for detecting the target analytes. Based on the preliminary analytical results, verification soil samples for WH-B01@6' (WH-B01R@6'), FL-B01@4' (FL-B01R@4'), and FL-B09@4' (FL-B09R@4') were collected on February 14 and 15, and March 6, 2024, and submitted for laboratory analysis of select Table 915-1 constituents that failed in the initial samples (benzene, 1-methylnaphthalene, pH, or select Table 915-1 metals [Cd, Pb, Se]). Laboratory analytical results received for the verification soil samples on March 26, 2024, confirmed that the cadmium (Cd), lead (Pb), and selenium (Se) concentrations in soil samples FL-B01@4' and FL-B01R@4' exceeded the ECMC Table 915-1 Protection of Groundwater Soil Screening Level Concentrations as well as the site-specific background levels (x 1.25). Final analytical results for the initial and/or confirmation soil samples indicate that the remaining constituent concentrations in the soil samples collected during wellhead cut and cap and flowline removal activities were in compliance with ECMC Table 915-1 standards and/or within the range of site-specific background levels (x 1.25 for metals). Groundwater was not encountered during wellhead cut and cap and flowline removal activities. Excavation and site assessment activities are ongoing and will be summarized in a forthcoming quarterly Form 27-Supplemental Site Investigation and Remediation Workplan under Remediation Project No. 33099 (Form 27 Document No. 403606445).
Root Cause: Historically impacted soil was discovered following cut and cap and wellhead flowline riser removal activities at the Inouye 11-31A wellhead location.
Preventative Measures: Site infrastructure has been removed and will not be replaced.

Area Depth Determined: Extents were determined by visible staining at the soil surface west of the Barrell Springs compressor unit (Site), as identified in Field Inspection Form Document 701103842. Visible staining extents were excavated until no stained or suspected impacted soils remained. The excavation was backfilled and a new compressor unit was installed. On April, 23, 2024, Entrada Consulting Group field scientist was onsite along with the original excavation crew to conduct additional investigation and to collect confirmation soil samples from the lateral and vertical extents of previous excavation activities. All excavation soil samples, as well as a waste characterization sample collected from the stockpile of soils removed from Site (see Operator Comments for additional details), were submitted to an accredited laboratory for analysis of full Table 915-1 constituents. Analytical laboratory results are pending. Analytical results will be provided on a subsequent Form 19 Supplemental with either a request to close the spill/release on the Form 19, or a request to close the spill/release onto an open Remediation Project for further remediation effort.
Root Cause:
Root cause is still under investigation pending laboratory analytical results to aid in determining the nature of the material that caused visible surface staining. 

After discussion with O&M field crew at this facility, it was determined that condensate was not utilized to clean the old unit, as SEI reported previously to ECMC in email correspondence; rather, SuperClean brand degreaser was used for cleaning the old compressor unit (see photolog). 

Based on process knowledge of gas compressors, as well as inventory of chemicals and fluids used at this gas compressor, it is suspected that the staining was caused by cumulative effects of O&M activities, such as routine compressor oil and coolant changes, resulting in small volumes of engine oil and/or coolant to escape accumulating over time into surface staining. See photolog for maintenance fluids used onsite. 

Incident and root cause determination may be amended in a subsequent Form 19 supplemental based on the full Table 915-1 laboratory results for soil samples collected from the vertical and horizontal extents of excavation, and from soil collected from the stockpile of suspected impacted soils removed from the staining area.
Preventative Measures:
The former gas compressor unit was replaced with a new gas compressor in April 2024. 

Field crew performing O&M operations at all SEI-owned facilities have been instructed on prevention of releases of any volume per Rule 902.a,b,c. and general housekeeping requirements and best practices.

SEI has reviewed and instructed all staff and contractors on ECMC reporting and regulatory requirements in general, and in specific for Rule 912.b.(1).G: A suspected or actual Spill or Release of any volume where the volume cannot be immediately determined, including a spill or release of any volume that daylights from the subsurface. 

SEI has reviewed and instructed all staff and contractors on proper disposal of E&P Waste, per Rule 905.a.(1). 

Finally, SEI has contracted a consultant specializing in E&P remediation and ECMC regulatory compliance to prevent future reporting and remediation errors.

Other Waste: Historical release of compressor motor oil
Spill Description: Field Inspection Form Document 701103842 provided a comment of "stained ground at compressor" on 11/02/2023. Strachan Exploration, Inc (SEI) removed the compressor unit and investigated the stained ground underneath. Less than 2 cubic yards of potentially impacted soil was removed using conventional excavation equipment, and a new compressor unit was installed.
Area Depth Determined: Extents were determined by visible staining at the soil surface west of the Barrell Springs compressor unit (Site), as identified in Field Inspection Form Document 701103842. Visible staining extents were excavated until no stained or suspected impacted soils remained. The excavation was backfilled and a new compressor unit was installed. On April, 23, 2024, Entrada Consulting Group field scientist was onsite along with the original excavation crew to conduct additional investigation and to collect confirmation soil samples from the lateral and vertical extents of previous excavation activities. All excavation soil samples, as well as a waste characterization sample collected from the stockpile of soils removed from Site (see Operator Comments for additional details), were submitted to an accredited laboratory for analysis of full Table 915-1 constituents to demonstrate the staining was caused by a refined non-E&P oil product, not indicative of condensate or production fluids.
Root Cause:
Field Inspection Form Document 701103842 provided a comment of "stained ground at compressor" on 11/02/2023. Strachan Exploration, Inc (SEI) removed the compressor unit and investigated the stained ground underneath. Less than 2 cubic yards of potentially impacted soil was removed using conventional excavation equipment, and a new compressor unit was installed.

Based on process knowledge of gas compressors, as well as inventory of chemicals and fluids present at this gas compressor, the staining noted in Inspection adjacent to the compressor was caused by non-E&P waste compressor motor oil. It is suspected that motor oil accumulated in and around the compressor unit during routine historical O&M activities, and when washed down with SuperClean while attempting to revive the old unit, caused fluids to wash onto the surrounding soils and cause surface staining.
Preventative Measures:
The former gas compressor unit was replaced with a new gas compressor in April 2024.

Field crew performing O&M operations at all SEI-owned facilities have been instructed on prevention of releases of any volume per
Rule 902.a,b,c. and general housekeeping requirements and best practices.

SEI has reviewed and instructed all staff and contractors on ECMC reporting and regulatory requirements in general, and in specific
for Rule 912.b.(1).G: A suspected or actual Spill or Release of any volume where the volume cannot be immediately determined,
including a spill or release of any volume that daylights from the subsurface.

SEI has reviewed and instructed all staff and contractors on proper disposal of E&P Waste, per Rule 905.a.(1).

Finally, SEI has contracted a consultant specializing in E&P remediation and ECMC regulatory compliance to prevent future
reporting and remediation errors.
Other Disposition Description: In containment tote at SEI storage facility, pending offsite disposal. See photolog.

Spill Description:
ECMC Staff conducted an inspection on November 29, 2023 (713600432) of the Frazee #2-6 (API# 05-061-06365), and observed impacted soils at the tank battery and oil stains on the tank due to a spill. Staff also observed disturbed surface soils that were spread over a large area around the tank battery; stained soils beneath the disturbed surface soils; and newly installed, loosely compacted, secondary containment around the tank battery. Staff notified Operator of the spill the day of the
inspection, November 29, 2023. Staff required corrective actions for Operator to immediately comply with the requirements of Rule 912 for a Spill or Release.
ECMC Staff conducted a follow-up inspection on February 27, 2024 (713600781), and Staff observed newly reconstructed berms that were constructed with impacted soils from the spill and emitting a hydrocarbon odor; visibly impacted soils freshly spread from the tank battery to the access road.
Area Depth Determined: Initially, extents will be determined as identified in NOAV Document 403806983, and from photos provided in Inspection photologs. Delineation of impacted material will be conducted via grab confirmation soil samples collected from surface and subsurface soils to determine the vertical and horizontal extents of impacts. Potentially impacted soils will be excavated using conventional excavation equipment, and transported to a waste disposal facility certified to dispose E&P waste. Grab confirmation samples will be collected from the final extents of excavation at a frequency that meets or exceeds ECMC Operator Guidance for Rule 915.e.(2) - Table 1 - Recommended minimum sample numbers based on excavation size. Soil samples will be submitted to a NELAP accredited laboratory for analysis of full Table 915-1 contaminant of concern for soils (and groundwater if encountered) until such time that a reduced sampling scope is proposed and approved by ECMC.
Additional Spill Details: Depth to water is estimated based on domestic water well permit 34544, mapped approximately 1 mile north of the location reporting a static water level of 83 feet below ground surface. Surface elevations report the Frazee 2-6 location is approximately 20 feet lower than is shown at the domestic well location.
Root Cause:
Witnesses to the initial release event (the landowner and the water hauler) reported that the pumping unit was shut down within 30 minutes of failure event. If the pump was running at full load capacity the spill was limited to 2-4bbls. Realistically the well makes 3.4 BOPD so 2 BBLS is highly unlikely in 30 minutes. The estimated volume is 0.5 bbl release, less than 5 bbls reporting threshold inside the containment.
Field personnel reported having addressed the initial spill. The impacted soil was moved to the edge of location for collection and transport to Otero landfill. In the meantime, SEI transported fresh soil to rebuild the berms. Unfortunately, our contractor blended the fresh soil w/ the impacted pile and rebuilt the berms and filled in areas of the road that had washed. 
This issue has been identified in NOAV Document 403806983
Preventative Measures: SEI has reviewed and instructed all staff and contractors on ECMC reporting, regulatory, and housekeeping requirements in general, and in specific for Rule 912.b.(1).G: A suspected or actual Spill or Release of any volume where the volume cannot be immediately determined, including a spill or release of any volume that daylights from the subsurface and Operator will submit an initial report (“24 hour notification”) of a Spill or Release of E&P Waste, natural gas, or produced fluids that meet any of the reporting criteria. SEI has contracted a consultant specializing in E&P remediation and ECMC regulatory compliance to prevent future reporting and remediation errors.

Spill Description:
ECMC Staff conducted an inspection on November 29, 2023 (713600432) of the Frazee #2-6 (API# 05-061-06365), and observed impacted soils at the tank battery and oil stains on the tank due to a spill. Staff also observed disturbed surface soils that were spread over a large area around the tank battery; stained soils beneath the disturbed surface soils; and newly installed, loosely compacted, secondary containment around the tank battery. Staff notified Operator of the spill the day of the
inspection, November 29, 2023. Staff required corrective actions for Operator to immediately comply with the requirements of Rule 912 for a Spill or Release.
ECMC Staff conducted a follow-up inspection on February 27, 2024 (713600781), and Staff observed newly reconstructed berms that were constructed with impacted soils from the spill and emitting a hydrocarbon odor; visibly impacted soils freshly spread from the tank battery to the access road.
Area Depth Determined: Initially, extents will be determined as identified in NOAV Document 403806983, and from photos provided in Inspection photologs. Delineation of impacted material will be conducted via grab confirmation soil samples collected from surface and subsurface soils to determine the vertical and horizontal extents of impacts. Potentially impacted soils will be excavated using conventional excavation equipment, and transported to a waste disposal facility certified to dispose E&P waste. Grab confirmation samples will be collected from the final extents of excavation at a frequency that meets or exceeds ECMC Operator Guidance for Rule 915.e.(2) - Table 1 - Recommended minimum sample numbers based on excavation size. Soil samples will be submitted to a NELAP accredited laboratory for analysis of full Table 915-1 contaminant of concern for soils (and groundwater if encountered) until such time that a reduced sampling scope is proposed and approved by ECMC.
Additional Spill Details: Depth to water is estimated based on domestic water well permit 34544, mapped approximately 1 mile north of the location reporting a static water level of 83 feet below ground surface. Surface elevations report the Frazee 2-6 location is approximately 20 feet lower than is shown at the domestic well location.
Root Cause:
Witnesses to the initial release event (the landowner and the water hauler) reported that the pumping unit was shut down within 30
minutes of failure event. If the pump was running at full load capacity the spill was limited to 2-4bbls. Realistically the well makes 3.4
BOPD so 2 BBLS is highly unlikely in 30 minutes. The estimated volume is 0.5 bbl release, less than 5 bbls reporting threshold inside
the containment.

SEI has contracted a consultant specializing in E&P remediation and ECMC regulatory compliance to prevent future reporting and remediation errors.
