Spill Description: On July 11, 2024, at 7:06 PM, a PSV lifted on the lean amine charcoal filter which flowed the excess amine into the amine sump tank. An estimated amount of approximately 8 barrels, overfilled out of the sump onto the ground. The amine traveled in a concrete ditch towards the west and south. Operations immediately dispatched a hydro-vac truck to the site to remove any free-standing liquids. The spill was under control by 8:38 PM. Additionally, Operations used a hotsy pressure washer and ~600 gallons of clean water to clean the area while the hydro-vac captured the wash water which was disposed of off-site at an approved disposal facility. Approximately 20 bbls of wash water and used amine was recovered. The spill was limited to the sump, rock, concrete culvert and rip-rap material at the inlet to a facility stormwater retention pond. The spilled material did not breach the culvert or the rip rap at the entrance to the retention pond and did not enter the retention pond.
Area Depth Determined: On July 11, 2024, at 7:06 PM, a PSV lifted on the lean amine charcoal filter which flowed the excess amine into the amine sump tank. An estimated amount of approximately 8 barrels, overfilled out of the sump onto the ground. The amine traveled from the sump to a concrete drainage ditch to the west and south. Operations immediately dispatched a hydro-vac truck to the site to remove any free-standing liquids. The spill was under control by 8:38 PM. Additionally, Operations used a hotsy pressure washer and approximately 600 gallons of clean water to clean the area around the sump, the concrete drainage, and the outfall rip rap while the hydro-vac captured the wash water which was disposed of off-site at an approved disposal facility. Approximately 20 bbls of wash water and used amine was recovered. The spill was limited to the amine sump, road base rock material, concrete drainage, and concreted rip rap material at the outfall and inlet to a facility stormwater retention pond. The spilled material did not breach the drainage or the rip rap at the entrance to the retention pond and did not enter the retention pond. The road base material around the sump and the rip rap material was also washed with the hotsy washer and wash water was recovered with hydro-vac equipment. The attached Figure 2 illustrates the flow path of the used amine spill from the sump to the outfall. A photographic log of the sump and used amine spill flow path is provided as an attachment. The facility SDS for amine is included as an attachment. This spill report is being submitted in accordance with Rule 912.b.(1).C.
Geology Description: Olney fine sandy loam, 1 to 3 percent slopes
Root Cause: On July 11, 2024, at 7:06 PM, a PSV lifted on the lean amine charcoal filter which flowed the excess amine into the amine sump tank. An estimated amount of approximately 8 barrels of used amine overfilled out of the sump onto the ground before equipment shutdown was completed. The amine traveled to a concrete ditch towards the west and south.
Preventative Measures: The PSV acted as designed and prevented over pressurization of the system. The PSV is tested in accordance with manufacturer specifications. All equipment operated as designed and the overflow was due to the amount of time between the PSV lifting and equipment shut-down.

Other Waste: Disconnection of hoses from blender to change to a new unit resulted in water run-off out of hoses.
Spill Description: Water being used for frac stimulation is a combination of 85% fresh water and 15% produced water (Fruitland Coal - CBM produced water).The main blender went down during the frac operations. During the disconnection of hoses from the primary blender to the standby blender, the hoses leaked-off water onto the ground. An estimated eight (8) barrels of water were discharged onto the ground. There were no hydrocarbons or chemicals associated with this spill. Initial clean-up of standing water to be picked up by sump truck.  The area will be covered with fill dirt (currently on location), sawdust and/or combination of both materials.  Once the completion operations is finished and equipment moved off of location, a final clean-up of the spill area and well pad will be initiated.  The final clean-up will be to excavate the spill area and replace the area with fill dirt that is presently located on the well pad.  The excavated dirt will be hauled off to the local landfill - Bondad Landfill.
Root Cause: Root Cause:  Operator on blender disconnected hoses from the blender and laid them on the ground without notifying a supervisor. This allowed the water to drain from the hoses onto the well site pad.
Preventative Measures:
Future Measures:  1.  If applicable, flush all hoses on blender with fresh water to working water tank prior to disconnecting hoses.
2. Install large catch pans and/or containment areas/tanks to drain hoses from stimulation equipment upon disconnection from equipment,
Note:  See operator comments for remedial work to be completed after completion operations are finished.

Spill Description: On May 22, 2024, an unknown volume of E&P exempt natural gas was released outside of containment from Pipeline 38-0000-5484-4. The release has been controlled, and excavation and site assessment activities are currently in progress, and will be summarized in a forthcoming Form 27-Supplemental update pending approval of Form 27-Initial Document No. 403874883.
Area Depth Determined: On May 22, 2024, an unknown volume of E&P exempt natural gas was released outside of containment from Pipeline 38-0000-5484-4. The release has been controlled. Excavation activities were initiated on July 2, 2024, and soil samples ware collected from the base and sidewalls of the release excavation area, and submitted for laboratory analysis of benzene, toluene, ethylbenzene, total xylenes (BTEX), 1,2,4 & 1,3,5-trimethlybenzene, and total petroleum hydrocarbons (TPH) using standard ECMC-approved methods appropriate for detecting the target analytes. Analytical results indicated that the benzene concentrations in soil sample REL-B01@3" exceeded the applicable ECMC Table 915-1 Protection of Groundwater Soil Screening Level Concentrations. The remaining VOC and TPH concentrations in soil samples collected on July 2, 2024 were in compliance with ECMC Table 915-1 standards. Excavation and site assessment activities are currently in progress, and will be summarized in a forthcoming Form 27-Supplemental update. Reference Supplemental Form 19 (Document No. 403821957) and pending Initial Form 27 (Document No. 403874883).
Geology Description: Vona loamy sand, 0 to 3 percent slopes
Root Cause: A release of E&P exempt natural gas was discovered from Pipeline 38-0000-5484-4 due to under-shielding coating corrosion at 6 o'clock on the line. The corrosion was potentially caused by joint weld decay, the concrete pad, dated construction standards, or the line being non-piggable and remaining in service due to contractual obligations. Excavation, site assessment, and site investigation activities into the root cause of this release activities are currently ongoing.
Preventative Measures: WES has evaluated the line for efficiencies and has repaired the line by cutting out the damaged section and replacing it with new line and pressure testing it. WES has many methods in place to prevent leaks and reoccurrence of leaks such as AVO, Aerial flights, pigging, chemical treatments and CP coupon reads.

The impacted soils were approximately 5 cubic yards. The well never produced or tested any oil and gas, and it is considered the impacted soil was a result of leakage from the drilling or workover rig motors. During the digging operations we segregated the impacted soil into a pile. We then found the extents of the impacted soil and dug a small buffer around to ensure complete clean up. The total area dug up was a circular area around the wellhead with an approximately 9 foot diameter.  The depth of the impacted soil was about 1 foot deep and 1-2 feet thick. Total soil excavated was approximately 5 cubic yards. The impacted soil has since been removed.
Geology Description: Impacted soil, clean soil and background soil samples were taken. The clean soil analytical data shows profile for natural geological soil.
Root Cause: The root cause of historic spill is unknown.
Preventative Measures: 24-hour notification to ECMC on any Spill or Release in which 1 Barrel or more of E&P Waste or produced Fluids is spilled or released outside of berms or other secondary containment. Immediately complete remediation of Spills or Releases. Implementation of Spill of Releases prevention policies.

Spill Description: On 1/15/24, a landowner reported noise at the Shoemaker 01-34 1 well site. The Fire Department responded and contacted SIMCOE. A gas release from a 3/8" tubing vent line was discovered due to a contractor failing to close a 1/2" valve after maintenance. SIMCOE remotely shut down the well, stopping the release. Approximately 20 mscf of gas was released after a 4 hr period. As the well produces 100% methane with minor amounts of entrained water, no liquid was spilled on the ground. No significant public or environmental hazards occurred, and the well was safely returned to service after assessments. Please refer to the attached "Shoemaker 01-34 1 NOAV 403888944_Answer_9.11.24.pdf" to the NOAV Document No. 403888944 for a comprehensive review of the events.
Root Cause: The 3rd party failed to close the vent valve after using it to blow down/purge the meter tube to inspect the orifice plate for a meter calibration.
Preventative Measures: The contractor did not adhere to the energy isolation policy outlined in our services agreement with the contractor. This policy mandates proper isolation procedures for tasks performed using flags and requires visibility and control over isolation points. The contractor’s management and training department addressed this lapse. Future compliance will be ensured through field audits and continued oversight.

Spill Description: On 9/30/2024, during removal of a DCP Operating, LP / Phillips 66 (DCP/P66) meter shed, an above ground valve leak was discovered at the meter shed which was connected to a 2-inch line that traveled down to a 90-degree bend connected to a horizontal 3-inch line. The meter shed, valve, and 2-inch line were removed, and the 3-inch line was capped. Condensate material traveled from the valve down the 2-inch line into the subsurface. On 9/30/2024, a “source area” soil sample was collected and submitted for laboratory analysis of the Table 915-1 list of analytes to evaluate potential impacts to the subsurface. Three background samples were also collected at the locations illustrated on Figure 2 and submitted for analysis of the Table 915-1 list of Metals and Soil Suitability analytes. Less than 10 cubic yards of soil were disturbed during initial investigation activities and this report is being submitted in accordance with Rule 912.b.(1).G.
Area Depth Determined: During removal of the meter shed, potentially impacted soil was observed at the surface below a valve that leaked and around a 2-inch line that traveled below ground to a 90-degree bend and a 3-inch horizontal line located approximately 2.5 feet below ground surface (bgs). The soil was field screened with a photoionization detector (PID) and a “source area” soil sample was collected at 2.5 feet bgs and submitted for laboratory analysis of the Table 915-1 list of analytes to determine petroleum hydrocarbon volatile organic compound (VOC), polyaromatic hydrocarbon (PAH), soil suitability, and metals concentrations in the spilled source material. Three background samples were also collected at the locations illustrated on Figure 2 and submitted for analysis of the Table 915-1 list of soil suitability and metals constituents of concern (COC). On 10/7/2024, the laboratory analytical results confirmed that impacted soil was above ECMC Table 915-1 standards. The results are summarized on the attached Tables 1 through 3 and provided in the laboratory analytical report. Based on the laboratory analytical results for the spilled material within the Source soil sample and the background concentrations, DCP/P66 proposes a site-specific soil sampling and analysis plan (SAP) provided in Table 4. Additional site investigation and remediation is planned to be performed using excavation and disposal methods.

A registered freshwater emergent wetland is located approximately 70 feet southeast, and a 4.1-acre freshwater pond is located approximately 500 feet northwest.

Spill Description: Field Inspection Form Document 701103842 provided a comment of "stained ground at compressor" on 11/02/2023. Strachan Exploration, Inc (SEI) removed the compressor unit and investigated the stained ground underneath. Less than 2 cubic yards of potentially impacted soil was removed using conventional excavation equipment, and a new compressor unit was installed.
Area Depth Determined:
Extents were determined by visible staining at the soil surface west of the Barrell Springs compressor unit (Site), as identified in Field Inspection Form Document 701103842. Visible staining extents were excavated until no stained or suspected impacted soils remained. The excavation was backfilled and a new compressor unit was installed. On April, 23, 2024, Entrada Consulting Group field scientist was onsite along with the original excavation crew to conduct additional investigation and to collect confirmation soil samples from the lateral and vertical extents of previous excavation activities. All excavation soil samples, as well as a waste characterization sample collected from the stockpile of soils removed from Site (see Operator Comments for additional details), were submitted to an accredited laboratory for analysis of full Table 915-1 constituents to demonstrate the staining was caused by a refined non-E&P oil product, not
indicative of condensate or production fluids.
Root Cause:
Field Inspection Form Document 701103842 provided a comment of "stained ground at compressor" on 11/02/2023. Strachan Exploration, Inc (SEI) removed the compressor unit and investigated the stained ground underneath. Less than 2 cubic yards of potentially impacted soil was removed using conventional excavation equipment, and a new compressor unit was installed.

Based on process knowledge of gas compressors, as well as inventory of chemicals and fluids present at this gas compressor, the
staining noted in Inspection adjacent to the compressor was caused by non-E&P waste compressor motor oil. It is suspected that
motor oil accumulated in and around the compressor unit during routine historical O&M activities, and when washed down with
SuperClean while attempting to revive the old unit, caused fluids to wash onto the surrounding soils and cause surface staining.
Preventative Measures:
The former gas compressor unit was replaced with a new gas compressor in April 2024.

Spill Description: On 9/30/2024, during removal of a DCP Operating, LP / Phillips 66 (DCP/P66) meter shed, an above ground valve leak was discovered at the meter shed connection to a 2-inch line that traveled down to a 90-degree bend connected to a horizontal 3-inch line. The meter shed, valve, and 2-inch line were removed, and the 3-inch line was capped. Condensate material traveled from the valve down the 2-inch line into the subsurface. On 9/30/2024, a “source area” soil sample was collected and submitted for laboratory analysis of the Table 915-1 list of analytes to evaluate potential impacts to the subsurface. Three background samples were also collected at the locations illustrated on Figure 2 and submitted for analysis of the Table 915-1 list of Metals and Soil Suitability analytes. Excavation was performed on 10/8/2024 and less than 10 cubic yards of soil were removed for disposal. Form 19-I w/S #403948663 was approved on 11/1/2024 and included a Site-Specific Sampling and Analysis Plan.
Area Depth Determined: During removal of the meter shed, impacted soil was observed at the surface below a valve that leaked around a 2-inch line that traveled below ground to a 90-degree bend and a 3-inch horizontal line located approximately 2.5 feet below ground surface (bgs). The soil was field screened with a photoionization detector (PID) and a “source area” soil sample was collected at 2.5 feet bgs and submitted for laboratory analysis of the Table 915-1 list of analytes to determine petroleum hydrocarbon volatile organic compound (VOC), polyaromatic hydrocarbon (PAH), soil suitability, and metals concentrations in the spilled source material. Three background samples were also collected at the locations illustrated on Figure 2 and submitted for analysis of the Table 915-1 list of soil suitability and metals constituents of concern (COC). On 10/7/2024, the laboratory analytical results confirmed that impacted soil was above ECMC Table 915-1 standards and based on the laboratory analytical results for the spilled material within the Source soil sample and the background concentrations, DCP/P66 proposed a site-specific soil sampling and analysis plan (SAP) provided in Table 4 included with approved Form 19-I w/S submittal #403948663 (11/1/2024). Excavation and disposal of impacted soil was completed on 10/8/2024 and soil samples were collected from the excavation extents illustrated in Figure 3. Because the Form 19-1 w/S was submitted on 10/8/2024, and ECMC did not have time to comment on the proposed SAP, soil samples from the excavation extents were submitted or full Table 915-1 laboratory soil analysis. The results are summarized on the attached Tables 1 through 3 and provided in the attached laboratory analytical report. Spill Description: On 12/31/2023 at roughly 6pm an Ignitor Tube (Separator) released 2 bbls of oil and 13 bbls of water due to failure caused by corrosion. Root Cause: Ignitor Tube (Separator) released 2 bbl of oil and 13 bbl of water due to failure caused by corrosion. Release was within unlined containment. The vessel was isolated, ignition sources were shut off, and all fluids (15 bbl) were recovered via hydrovac.
Preventative Measures: In September 2024, a one-time batch treatment of 10 gallons of corrosion/scale inhibitor was completed at the Haley, Markham, Litzenberger, and Vail pads, with 5-gallon treatments completed on each well once every 4 weeks. Other pads were already receiving chemical to prevent failures like this. Cub Creek (1876) selected two wells per pad (one Niobrara, one Codell) and installs coupons in the process flow which are removed, tested, and replaced each quarter to monitor the corrosion rate and adjust chemical treatments schedules as needed. The coupons are sent to the chemical manufacturer (Valence) for analysis to ensure the corrosion/scale inhibitor treatments implemented at the Haley, Markham, Litzenberger, and Vail pads is the appropriate product to prevent failures like this in the future.

Since that time we have discovered the heater was only 5 years old so we are in touch with the manufacturer to see if the fire tube was faulty.
Root Cause:
The Briggsdale fire department notified Luke Crumley ( pumper for Redhawk) of a fire at the Staudinger facility. Another pumper in the 
area had already gone in and shut the well in. They quickly extinguished the fire and Mr. Crumley arrived at the lcoation early the next

Spill Description:
On January 2, 2025 KPK was notified a crude oil leak coming from a separator located at the Hazel McHale facility & had impacted the surficial soil within the separator's 
secondary containment. KPK responded & repaired the leaking separator.  The ECMC performed an inspection on January 10, 2020 (doc# 717100074) & noted that the impacted soil had not been remediated & collected three soil samples from within the release area. The samples were submitted for the full Table 915.1.  Those sample results indicated that both organic & inorganic impacts are above Table 915.1.  KPK was on-site on January 30, 2025 to begin excavating the contaminated soil.  At that time the release appeared to be less than one barrel (not reportable) however, after field screening and further investigation it appears that this is a historical release.  Approximately 10 cubic yards of contaminated soil has been excavated at the time of this submittal.  Remediation efforts are on-going.

Spill Description: In October 2023, Western Midstream (WES) contacted PDC Energy, Inc. (PDC), to inform Chevron of a discovery of contaminated soil that they believed to be a separate historical release in an area just south of the WES meter building.  On June 25, 2024, WES reached out to PDC to satisfy a condition of approval of its Form 27.  Based on the email and subsequent discussions, PDC committed to undertaking a Limited Site Assessment (LSA) to evaluate the potential source of the identified contaminated soil and extent of potential impacts.  The LSA was completed in August 2024 and the results identified the presence of historic hydrocarbons south and southeast of WES’s spill point.  The responsible party has not yet been identified.  As a result, a facility/location is not currently known, and a historic spill point has not been identified.  Although the responsible party has not yet been identified, PDC will be submitting an initial Form 27 consistent with ECMC’s September 17, 2024 request.
Area Depth Determined: This is a preliminary estimate. Estimated extent of hydrocarbon impacts identified south and southeast of WES's spill point are based on the results from the Limited Site Assessment (LSA), completed in August 2024. The extent is subject to change based on the receipt of additional information.
Additional Spill Details: On September 12, 2024, MW-7 was resampled to confirm groundwater hydrocarbon detections from the August 15, 2024 sampling event. Upgradient groundwater sample results for MW-5 and MW-6 were below Table 915-1 clean-up standards and less than the reporting limit for hydrocarbons, respectively. Additionally, the soil sample results for MW-7 were less than the reporting limit for Table 915-1 hydrocarbons but reported groundwater benzene concentrations as 7.3 ug/L. Based on these reported analysis and results, PDC resampled MW-7 to evaluate benzene concentrations in MW-7. Quarterly groundwater monitoring for the monitoring well network for Table 915-1 constituents is ongoing. Analytical data shall be submitted in a subsequent Form 27.
Root Cause: Historical impacts were discovered south and southeast of the WES meter building. Due to the historical nature of the release, an exact cause was not able to be identified.
Preventative Measures: This facility is no longer active and has been decommissioned. The unidentified source of the release was taken out of service at the time of decommissioning; therefore, there is no longer a possibility of a release originating from this location.

A reportable release occurred on 12/9/2024 at the Grigsby AC19-62HN facility. An unknown volume of freshwater and residual produced fluids daylighted to the surface during a hydrostatic test of the flowline associated with the Grigsby PC AC #30-73HN wellhead. The exact location where the flowline is compromised is currently under investigation. The release has been controlled and clean up and repair operations are scheduled to begin 1/17/2025. The release area lies within the Mule Deer Severe Winter Range and Pronghorn Winter Concentration High Priority Habitats.
Area Depth Determined: The vertical and horizontal extent of contamination will initially be determined via in field screening techniques using a photoionization device (PID) to measure volatile organic compounds as well as visual and olfactory observations. Excavation and soil sampling activities will be conducted to confirm the extent of impacts have been delineated. Soil samples will be submitted to an accredited laboratory and analyzed for ECMC Table 915-1 constituents to ensure the removal of all impacted material.
Additional Spill Details: No additional spill details.
Root Cause: This release occurred during a hydrostatic test of the flowline associated with the Grigsby PC AC #30-73HN wellhead. The exact location where the flowline is compromised is currently under investigation. The reason for failure is likely due to corrosion.
Preventative Measures: Upon discovering the source of the release, the compromised section of flowline will be replaced with new material. Additionally, chevron conducts annual integrity tests on all production lines. Further, if corrosion is deemed to be the cause of the release, Chevron will evaluate the effectiveness of using a chemical corrosion inhibitor to mitigate corrosion within lines.

Spill Description: In October 2023, Western Midstream (WES) contacted PDC Energy, Inc. (PDC), to inform Chevron of a discovery of contaminated soil that they believed to be a separate historical release in an area just south of the WES meter building.  On June 25, 2024, WES reached out to PDC to satisfy a condition of approval of its Form 27.  Based on the email and subsequent discussions, PDC committed to undertaking a Limited Site Assessment (LSA) to evaluate the potential source of the identified contaminated soil and extent of potential impacts.  The LSA was completed in August 2024 and the results identified the presence of historic hydrocarbons south and southeast of WES’s spill point.  The responsible party has not yet been identified.  As a result, a facility/location is not currently known, and a historic spill point has not been identified.  Although the responsible party has not yet been identified, PDC has submitted an initial Form 27 consistent with ECMC’s September 17, 2024 request.
Area Depth Determined: This is a preliminary estimate. Estimated extent of hydrocarbon impacts identified south and southeast of WES's spill point are based on the results from the Limited Site Assessment (LSA), completed in August 2024. The extent is subject to change based on the receipt of additional information. A description of further investigation and remediation of impacts is outlined in Initial Form 27, document number 404069471.
Additional Spill Details: Quarterly groundwater monitoring for the monitoring well network for Table 915-1 constituents is ongoing. Analytical data shall be submitted in a subsequent Form 27.
Root Cause:
Historical impacts were discovered south and southeast of the WES meter building. Due to the historical nature of the release, an 
exact cause was not able to be identified.
Preventative Measures:
This facility is no longer active and has been decommissioned. The unidentified source of the release was taken out of service at the 
time of decommissioning; therefore, there is no longer a possibility of a release originating from this location.

Spill Description: A reportable release occurred on 12/9/2024 at the Grigsby AC19-62HN facility. An unknown volume of freshwater and residual produced fluids daylighted to the surface during a hydrostatic test of the flowline associated with the Grigsby PC AC #30-73HN wellhead. The release has been controlled and clean up and repair operations are underway. The release area lies within the Mule Deer Severe Winter Range and Pronghorn Winter Concentration High Priority Habitats.
Area Depth Determined: Six soil borings (SB-1 8 Ft thru SB-6 8 Ft) were advanced to depths ranging from 4'-8' below ground surface (BGS) on 1/22/25 to determine the approximate extent of soil impacts prior to excavation operations. Seven soil samples were collected and submitted for full Table 915-1 analyses to Summit Scientific Inc. in Golden, Colorado. Laboratory analytical data indicated several organic, metals and inorganic exceedances. Remedial excavation will be required to remove soil impacts. Soil samples will be collected and analyzed for full Table 915-1 analyses to confirm soil impacts have been adequately remediated.
Additional Spill Details: A description of further investigation and remediation of impacts is outlined in Initial Form 27, document number 404102320.
Root Cause: This release occurred during a hydrostatic test of the flowline associated with the Grigsby PC AC #30-73HN wellhead. The failure point of the flowline was at a weld that did not get properly primed and tape and is thus a result of human error.
Preventative Measures: The compromised section of flowline will be replaced with new material upon the completion of remediation operations. Moving forward, Noble has reinstated the standard operating procedures for welding and flowline installation operations to the appropriate business partners to prevent this issue from reoccurring.

On 2/3/2025, the ECMC conducted an inspection of the pad location (reference inspection doc #718700031) and observed fluid in the Castor 7-59 10-3-5 mousehole and incorrectly assumed the fluid was pooled hydrocarbons. Upon further inspection, it was determined that the fluid in the mousehole was water from recent snowmelt. The observed water in the mousehole resulting from snowmelt appeared dark due to the water being very clear and the casing set inside of the mousehole being black. The water was immediately vacuumed (volume of <5 gallons) and the mousehole has been backfilled.

On 02/26/2025, the ECMC conducted an additional inspection (doc #718700134) and observed hydrocarbon staining immediately adjacent to the rat/mouse hole and documented a hydrocarbon olfactory sense from the stained material. Field screening of the hydrocarbon stained material indicated a PID reading of 12.7ppm (VOC). It was determined that additional clean up and remediation was necessary.
Area Depth Determined: The extent of surface impact is estimated to be <5 square feet based on arial measurements. The depth of impact is still being determined. The confirmed area will be provided with the next supplemental Form 19.
Root Cause: It is suspected that the soil surrounding the mousehole has been impacted by drilling mud percolating up from the mousehole. Clean up and remediation has begun. The free fluid observed within the mousehole was immediately vacuumed up and was determined to be < 5 gallons of freshwater from snowmelt. The mousehole has since been backfilled and there is no other free fluid present. The surrounding impacted soil is currently being excavated, and the excavated soil volume will be provided with the next Form 19 submittal.
Preventative Measures: The surrounding impacted soil is currently being excavated. Any remaining drill fluid found will be removed. Mousehole will be properly backfilled/ buried.

Historical impacts were discovered during tank battery decommissioning activities beneath the produced water vessel. Due to the

Noble conducts routine AVO inspections of all oil and gas facilities in order to identify and mitigate potential releases. Further, this

Other Waste: Detection of thermogenic methane in October 21, 2024 water well 773349 sample.
Spill Description: Consistent with Rule 615 in advance of drilling of Chatfield Federal 4N66W34 (facility ID 485574), baseline water quality samples were collected. Analytical results for Sample ID 773349 indicated total methane concentrations greater than 1.0 mg/L. Gas compositional analysis samples indicate the water sample contained thermogenic methane. Based on currently available information, there is insufficient data to determine whether the detected methane is associated with a spill/release attributable to oil & gas activities. Similarly, there is insufficient data to determine whether the potential source of the thermogenic methane has been stopped, contained, or recovered. Because the Form 19 requires a response regarding whether the spill/release has been controlled (and unknown is not an option), we have selected Yes. We will notify the ECMC if additional data becomes available suggesting otherwise. Available data suggests the presence of naturally occurring coal seams in the area.

The release was identified during an ECMC Inspection Report #713601401.  The small oil stained area by the loadout was determined to be less than 1 barrel of crude oil outside of containment. Stained soil around the load-out pipe was excavated and removed.
Area Depth Determined: The horizontal extent of impacts was determined via observations of surface soil staining. Further evaluation of impacts was determined by horizontal and vertical delineation via in field soil screening using a photoionization device (PID) during excavation and confirmation soil sampling.
Geology Description:
According to the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Soil Survey, the spill area is made up one soil type: Keith-Ulysses silt loams. The native composition of this soil type is:

 Symbol 20 (100% of area)
 Ap - 0 to 6 inches: silt loam
 Bt1 - 6 to 10 inches: silty clay loam
 Bt2 - 10 to 25 inches: silty clay loam
 C - 25 to 79 inches: silt loam
Additional Spill Details:
According to DWR records, the closest water well in proximity to the location (Permit 149694 ~ 3466 feet to the west) with data available had a reported static water depth of 220 feet BGS.

The location is within the CPW Rule 1202.c NSO Habitats for Aquatic Native Species Conservation Waters which is ~ 5,195 feet NW of the location.
Root Cause: This incident is the result of poor housekeeping and loadout procedures. Production operations had inadequate best management practices and necessary resources established to complete routine inspections and internal reporting/response to spills.
Preventative Measures: New procedures have been developed and implemented to complete routine inspections and reporting for locations field wide. Citation will be instituting a good-housekeeping action item priority list and maintenance schedule to address issues before they occur and begin replacing missing or aging equipment as possible. Failed or missing equipment is being replaced with more applicable alternatives in consideration of best engineering practices for longevity and site conditions.
